narration_timeline.text: Why is this great egret perched on branches instead of standing in the water?
narration_timeline.scene: Egret clearly perched on branches above wetland vegetation.

narration_timeline.text: Long legs let it wade through shallows while keeping its white body above the surface.
Across wetlands, it changes position slowly, sometimes appearing as a distant white speck among the reeds.
narration_timeline.scene: Wetland establishing view and distant egret; do not claim a strike.

narration_timeline.text: Its pointed bill and long neck help it watch for prey without plunging underwater.
narration_timeline.scene: Close profile of egret bill and neck, avoid embedded title segment.

narration_timeline.text: At a Florida wildlife park, egrets were even filmed standing on captive alligators.
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic captive alligator perch at Florida wildlife park.

narration_timeline.text: Whether wading or perching, this bird keeps a clear view of the water below.
narration_timeline.scene: Two distinct wading-egret scenes, no false same-location claim.
